name: DeepSeek
description: The DeepSeek R1/V3 family are production-oriented, open-weight Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs engineered for high reasoning throughput and cost-efficient scaling.

inference_notes: MoE activation sparsity reduces per-token FLOPs but requires expert routing and reliable load-balancing; DeepSeek implements loss-free load balancing and MLA to compress KV state, which materially reduces KV cache overhead on inference.
deployment_notes: For V3, use MoE-aware sharding and high-throughput interconnects (NVLink/NCCL) along with runtimes such as vLLM or vendor-optimized TensorRT pipelines; distills are the recommended path for simpler deployments.
optimization_notes: Mixed precision (FP8/FP16) micro-scaling and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) speculative decoding were used in training to improve throughput; evaluate FP8/FP16 inference carefully against reasoning quality regressions.
compatibility_notes: Distills convert well to GGUF/GPTQ for llama.cpp and other lightweight runtimes; full V3 requires MoE-supported runtimes and may need custom integration work for MLA and expert routing.
common_pitfalls: Pitfall: Treating V3 like a dense model — mitigation: provision MoE-aware runtime, test load balancing and routing across shards before production rollout.
Pitfall: Quantizing R1 without RL-quality validation — mitigation: run reasoning benchmarks post-quantization to validate chain-of-thought and correctness.

license_info.name: MIT / Open-source licenses applied per checkpoint
license_info.notes: Always validate license terms in the official model card before redistribution or commercial use.

best_for: High-quality reasoning and chain-of-thought agent systems where cost-per-query must be reduced via MoE activations.
Research and open-weight deployments that require reproducible RL-based reasoning models.
Self-hosted inference with MoE-aware runtimes (vLLM) to balance throughput and cost.
avoid_for: Simple, low-complexity deployments where MoE orchestration overhead outweighs activation savings. Use dense distills instead.
Strict latency SLOs on single-GPU commodity hardware for large V3 checkpoints without aggressive quantization or sharding strategies.
Environments that cannot accept open-weight licenses or require vendor-locked support.
engineering_snapshot.recommended_use_case: Use R1 distills (14B–70B) for most production reasoning workloads; reserve full V3 for workloads that require maximal open-weight capacity.
